To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel approach for sonic event generation, based on mathematical functions, and that this approach is suitable for use in a wide range of contexts, including authentication systems.

(i) the use of sound in authentication systems can be a powerful and pragmatic means for enhancing security, (ii) the use of musical elements in the design of sound-based authentication systems can be used to increase memorability, pleasure, and pragmatics, and (iii) the use of a mathematical function to generate the sound can be a useful and powerful approach for designing sound-based authentication systems.
a novel application for sound events has been designed, implemented and tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of musical sequences that are both pleasing and memorable.
the generation of musical sound events in a manner which is both musically pleasing and pragmatically appropriate to the context in which it is to be used.

the generation of sonics via mathematical functions implemented in Java; the application of these generative techniques for the purpose of authentication; the use of familiar musical dimensions in order to enhance memorability, pleasure, pragmatics and aesthetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is a pragmatic and musically pleasing production system for sonic events.
our approach is a pragmatic one, that it is musically pleasing, that it is based upon mathematical functions and that it is implemented on the universal Java platform.
our approach has the potential of being a viable alternative to alphanumeric and other password based authentication systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to produce a pragmatic, musically pleasing and aesthetically pleasing sound system.
we present a novel application for sonification and musical aesthetics namely their generation via a mathematical function.
it is a pragmatic and musically pleasing production system for sonic events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a novel and practical approach to generating sonics is possible.
the use of sound as a means for authentication is feasible.
the musical domain can be used as a rich source for the design of sonification systems.
